title: How a catalyst lowers the energy barrier
examples: Is a catalyst used up in a reaction?
What does a catalytic converter do?

explain.say: Imagine pushing a heavy cart over a tall hill to reach the other side. What if someone dug a tunnel through it? That is what a catalyst does for a reaction! Look at the board. This graph shows you the energy hill of a reaction.

draw.text: How a catalyst lowers the energy barrier

explain.say: See the top of the hill? That is the activation energy, the minimum energy particles need to react. Most collisions do not have enough to get over, so the reaction is slow. What would happen if you made the hill lower?

More particles get over! Look at the right side. A catalyst gives the reaction a different route with a lower hill. More collisions succeed, so it speeds up. The start and end stay exactly the same. Do you think the catalyst gets used up?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Same start, same end, lower hill

explain.say: No! Look at the cycle. Reactants stick to the catalyst, react, and leave as products. The catalyst is free to start again, unchanged, so a tiny amount works over and over. Can you think of a catalyst inside your own body?

Enzymes! Brilliant. Enzymes are nature's catalysts; one in your saliva starts breaking down rice and bread. Wow: a car's catalytic converter uses platinum to turn poisonous carbon monoxide into carbon dioxide in a split second.

faq.a: A catalyst is a substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up. It can be used again and again.
A catalyst provides a different route for the reaction with a lower activation energy. More collisions have enough energy, so the reaction goes faster.
asks: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?

faq.a: No. The catalyst is chemically the same at the end of the reaction, so only a small amount is needed.
asks: Does a catalyst change in a reaction?

faq.a: Enzymes are biological catalysts made of protein. Amylase in your saliva speeds up breaking starch into sugar.

faq.q: How does a catalytic converter work?
faq.a: It has a honeycomb coated in metals like platinum, palladium and rhodium. They speed up reactions that turn carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides and unburnt fuel into less harmful gases.
asks: What does a car's catalytic converter do?

facts: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by providing an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy, and is not used up.
Iron is the catalyst in the Haber process for making ammonia.

quiz.why: It gives a route with a lower activation energy.

wrong.0: Mass is conserved; a catalyst does not change it.
wrong.2: The products are the same with or without a catalyst.

quiz.say: Why is only a small amount of catalyst needed?
quiz.show: Why is only a small amount of catalyst needed?
quiz.why: The catalyst is left unchanged, so it can be reused over and over.

wrong.1: Its weight has nothing to do with it; it is reused.
